::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 22  [1894?]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MS English Letters: e.174 ff 173-4
:::

Dear [Mr Bullock](people/person_221.qmd),
Here is Salisbury. I am sorry I could find no more to say about it, the cathedral having been all built at once, and the Bishops not having been memorable except the last four.[^1] Burnet I could not put in![^2] The sunshine on the Altar on the 15th of August is quite true. I have seen it twice

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY refers to the work she was doing for Bullock's *Daily Lections* project. The last four Bishops of Salisbury had been [Edward Denison](people/person_2137.qmd), [Walter Kerr Hamilton](people/person_2138.qmd), [George Moberly](people/person_1015.qmd) and [John Wordsworth](people/person_1567.qmd), all High Churchmen.
[^2]: Gilbert Burnet (1643-1715) was probably both too worldly and too Low Church to please CMY.
